parsed.explanation: No traveller-facing universal exposure (border, facilities, custody) is documented; those axes are open questions, not safety. The heaviest documented facts are: a latent same-sex criminal exposure (unequal age of consent, 5–10 years) that reaches a trans visitor with an under-21 counterparty but not a heterosexual one; a documented concealment culture (2024) with coded networks; state cancellation of an LGBTQ event for 'debauchery'; and the 2025 government rejection of anti-violence and hate-speech recommendations — endorsing impunity with thin recourse. Anti-gender-nonconforming violence is documented only in a 2011 post-coup report (dated, including murder of trans sex workers). Data-protection statutes are a mild positive. Structural signals (social hostility + state tolerance + conditional criminalisation, no documented protections) place this at the Elevated boundary.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. Passport markers, visa practice and screening are explicitly excluded from the inventory; no friction or acceptance is evidenced either way.
entry_documents.interaction: Any document-presentation mismatch would interact with an undocumented screening regime — an open question, not an exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Article 331: same-sex acts with a person under 21 punishable as indecent assault, 5–10 years; also 2–5 years for 'indecent or against nature' acts. Unequal age of consent creates criminal exposure a heterosexual visitor lacks.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Same-sex conduct is lawful between adults 21+, so ordinary adult conduct is not criminal; no documented arrest of a visitor.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor travelling with a partner or companion under 21 converts a social-conservatism risk into criminal exposure; custody placement practice is not documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No facility, ward, custody-placement or gendered-space rule appears in the record.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: An emergency or detention would interact with unrecorded placement practice — uncertainty, not evidenced harm.

care_services.exposure: No trans-specific care access documented; health framing is HIV-only (Act 2005-040), with no visitor-facing denial recorded.
care_services.protection: Law 2014-038 Art.18 and Law 2017-045 Art.2 bar processing/ disclosure of health, sexual-life and sexual-orientation data — a genuine, if indirect, anti-outing protection.
care_services.interaction: Data protections constrain disclosure by controllers but do not reach informal social outing.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Government cancelled a 2021 LGBTQ party for 'incitement to debauchery' and in Jan 2025 rejected recommendations to combat anti-LGBT violence and hate speech — state-endorsed impunity, not merely private prejudice.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No documented state-directed arrest campaign, moral police or registration of trans people.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State refusal to act removes recourse from street-level hostility, elevating social hostility above friction.

minors_guardians.exposure: Unequal age of consent (21 for same-sex acts, 5–10 years) directly reaches an adult travelling with or accompanied by a minor/under-21 person; religious leaders offered conversion therapy to a 19-year-old in the 2020 case.
minors_guardians.protection: Adoption and marriage restrictions are resident-facing and do not touch a visiting guardian.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family's mixed-status or same-sex context converts into criminal and social exposure simultaneously.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2014-era? no: 2011 foreign report recorded verbal abuse, stone-throwing and murder of gender-nonconforming people (trans sex workers prominent), plus social-media death threats to supporters of a same-sex couple (undated); Aug 2024 report documents concealment to live in peace.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No post-2011 documented anti-trans violence; absence in a thin record is not proof of safety.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Dated violence plus a current concealment culture and rejected anti-violence recommendations indicate hostility with thin recourse rather than a current campaign.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Government rejection (2025) of anti-violence and hate-speech measures; local groups call it endorsing impunity — oversight working against, not for, LGBT people.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Six named local organisations, case law and protection machinery are referenced as existing elsewhere; data-protection statutes give a nominal complaint route.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper and civil-society recourse coexist with state refusal, so remedies are thin and slow for a short-stay visitor.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A: Vellandra has a universal, routine administrative exclusion regime reaching every trans visitor at the border. This dossier documents no traveller-facing universal measure — no screening, registration or reporting rule — only a conditional criminal statute and social/state hostility with thin recourse.

Similar in kind but different in mechanism: Kestrel Isles' exposure is documented, routine border secondary screening with uncertain outcomes. Here the analogous border friction is not_documented; the documented weight sits on latent criminal exposure and endorsed impunity, making severity higher but universality lower.

Below 0.75-C: Meridia documents trained border officers, tribunal appeal, compensation and lawful entry on presentation-matched documents. This record documents the opposite climate — event bans, rejection of anti-violence recommendations, concealment culture — with no documented protection machinery for visitors.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is one of documented social hostility tolerated and partly endorsed by the state, without any documented universal traveller-facing mechanism. The concrete criminal exposure is narrow and conditional (same-sex acts with under-21s, 5–10 years) but real and trans/same-sex-specific; the state's 2021 party ban and 2025 rejection of anti-violence recommendations convert private hostility into tier-3 hostility with thin recourse. Anti-trans violence is evidenced only by a 2014-year-old? 2011 post-coup report including murder — dated, not current frequency, and not proof of cessation. Missing border, facility and custody documentation are open questions, not safety; data-protection statutes offer a modest anti-outing safeguard. Net: Elevated Risk at the Reduced boundary.
